Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: Open-CHOIR: Open-World Contact-Aware 4D Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Hao Xu, Yilin Liu, Yinqiao Wang, Chi-Wing Fu, Niloy J. Mitra
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: Open-CHOIR is a framework that reconstructs 4D hand-object interactions from monocular videos by utilizing contact as a coupling signal for improved accuracy and consistency.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: We ask whether everyday open-world monocular videos can be turned into reusable 4D interaction primitives: articulated hand motion, object shape with 6D pose over time, and the when/where of contact. Such a capability would enable scalable mining of real interactions and, beyond reconstruction, support scene-aware synthesis and planning. However, reconstructing hand-object interaction (HOI) from challenging monocular videos remains difficult: methods often assume known objects or curated scenes, and separately estimated hands and objects easily become misaligned under clutter, occlusion, and unseen object geometries. Targeting this setting, we present Open-CHOIR, an Open-world Contact-aware HOI Reconstruction framework for a monocular camera, using contact as an explicit coupling signal between hands and objects. Open-CHOIR first initializes a coarse, contact-agnostic 4D HOI sequence from open-world visual priors. It then introduces a generative HOI spatial rectification module to predict ray-depth corrections and rectify hand-object relative placement, then derive initial per-frame contact correspondences on the rectified geometry. Last, a contact-aware joint optimization with dynamically updated contact constraints enforces geometric, temporal, and contact consistency. Experiments on controlled and challenging videos show that Open-CHOIR improves object reconstruction, physical plausibility, and temporal consistency over state-of-the-art methods. Code, data, and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/hxwork/CHOIR.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: Boosting Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Deep Reinforcement Learning
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Zexin Li, Ruili Yao, Yiming Zeng, Xiaoxue Gao
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: This paper presents a trajectory-level black-box attack method for deep reinforcement learning that outperforms traditional per-step attacks by optimizing observation perturbations over time.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Most adversarial attacks on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) assume white-box access to the victim policy, which rarely holds in practice. This paper studies transfer-based black-box attacks on DRL: the attacker crafts observation perturbations on a white-box surrogate agent and feeds them to an unknown victim. We formulate the attack as return minimization under a per-step perturbation budget. We first show that transplanting transferable image-classification attacks (FGSM, MI-FGSM, and NI-FGSM) with a per-step objective yields perturbations that transfer but are no stronger than random noise of the same budget. We then propose a trajectory-level attack that optimizes a sequence of perturbations over a receding horizon through a differentiable model of the environment and a temperature-smoothed surrogate policy, with the same optimizers. On CartPole-v1 with ten DQN and DDQN agents and 100 surrogate--victim pairs, the trajectory-level attack outperforms per-step attacks and random noise in the white-box, cross-model, and cross-algorithm settings.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: $R^2$-WAM: Repair-and-Reject Post-Training for World Action Models
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Ruiyan Xu, Haisheng Su, Sixu Lin, Zhaokun Yue, Chengming Hu
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: $R^2$-WAM enhances World Action Models by implementing a two-stage repair-and-reject framework to improve action prediction consistency and refine policies without extra interactions.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) emerge as a promising foundation for policy refinement by predicting the consequences of sampled actions. On the long-horizon real-world Fold Shirt task, it achieves 87.5% average success, compared with 0% for Fast-WAM. Our project page is available at https://r2-wam.github.io/.

OpenDriveLab.title: TriDeliver: Cooperative Air-Ground Instant Delivery with UAVs, Couriers, and Crowdsourced Ground Vehicles
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Junhui Gao, Yan Pan, Qianru Wang, Wenzhe Hou, Yiqin Deng
OpenDriveLab.summary: TriDeliver introduces a hierarchical framework combining UAVs, couriers, and crowdsourced ground vehicles, enhancing instant delivery efficiency and reducing costs significantly through transfer learning.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Instant delivery, shipping items before critical deadlines, is essential in daily life. While multiple delivery agents, such as couriers, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), and crowdsourced agents, have been widely employed, each of them faces inherent limitations (e.g., low efficiency/labor shortages, flight control, and dynamic capabilities, respectively), preventing them from meeting the surging demands alone. This paper proposes TriDeliver, the first hierarchical cooperative framework, integrating human couriers, UAVs, and crowdsourced ground vehicles (GVs) for efficient instant delivery. To obtain the initial scheduling knowledge for GVs and UAVs as well as improve the cooperative delivery performance, we design a Transfer Learning (TL)-based algorithm to extract delivery knowledge from couriers' behavioral history and transfer their knowledge to UAVs and GVs with fine-tunings, which is then used to dispatch parcels for efficient delivery. Evaluated on one-month real-world trajectory and delivery datasets, it has been demonstrated that 1) by integrating couriers, UAVs, and crowdsourced GVs, TriDeliver reduces the delivery cost by $65.8\%$ versus state-of-the-art cooperative delivery by UAVs and couriers; 2) TriDeliver achieves further improvements in terms of delivery time ($-17.7\%$), delivery cost ($-9.8\%$), and impacts on original tasks of crowdsourced GVs ($-43.6\%$), even with the representation of the transferred knowledge by simple neural networks, respectively.

OpenDriveLab.title: MagCilia: A Compact Magnetociliary Tactile Sensor with 3D Force Sensing for Robotic Contact Perception and Grasping Feedback
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Yu Feng, Hao Wu, Haotian Guo, Haoming Liu, William Su
OpenDriveLab.summary: The MagCilia sensor enables precise 3D force sensing and surface recognition for robotic grasping through a compact design integrating flexible magnetic-cilia structures and advanced data fusion techniques.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Robotic grasping and surface exploration benefit from simultaneous measurement of normal and tangential forces and from surface information obtained through contact. Here, we present a compact magnetociliary tactile sensor (MagCilia) that combines a flexible magnetic-cilia structure with a Hall sensor for 3D force sensing. Quasi-static finite element analysis is used to investigate structural deformation and magnetic responses under multidirectional loading. To reconstruct forces from the coupled magnetic channels, we propose causal history fusion regression (CHFR), which combines current magnetic-field measurements with their recent changes. Five-fold cross-validation grouped by calibration record yields root-mean-square errors of 0.40, 0.57, and 0.69 N for Fx, Fy, and Fz, respectively, with corresponding coefficients of determination of 0.93, 0.90, and 0.92. Robotic experiments demonstrate tangential-force-guided gripper adjustment and multi-axis load monitoring under external perturbations. Frequency-domain features of the reconstructed forces distinguish six surface categories with 99.39% accuracy in three-fold cross-validation grouped by acquisition session. An online robotic demonstration additionally identifies all six tested surfaces. These results demonstrate 3D force reconstruction, grasping feedback, and surface recognition using a single compact tactile unit.

OpenDriveLab.title: Not All Uncertainty Matters: Simulation-in-the-Loop Fast-Slow Reasoning for Decision-Critical Autonomous Driving System
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Jiayi Chen, Shuai Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Chengzhong Xu
OpenDriveLab.summary: The paper presents SIGMA, a simulation-in-the-loop framework that optimizes cloud interactions for autonomous driving by assessing uncertainty's impact on planning efficiency and decision-making.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) provide powerful open-world perception and reasoning for autonomous driving, but their high computational cost and inference latency make continuous cloud-side use impractical. This motivates fast--slow collaboration, where efficient onboard modules handle real-time perception and control while cloud models provide high-level reasoning only when needed. The key challenge is deciding when cloud reasoning should influence time-critical driving decisions. Existing methods often rely on perception uncertainty, heuristic triggers, or resource-driven policies, without assessing whether resolving an uncertainty will improve planning. We propose \textbf{SIGMA}, a simulation-in-the-loop framework for task-oriented fast--slow collaboration. SIGMA embeds the planner into uncertainty assessment and evaluates how plausible scene realizations under semantic and geometric uncertainty affect feasible trajectories and planning cost. Based on these outcomes, it estimates the expected reduction in planning cost from resolving uncertainty. We further introduce expected planning gain (EPG), a decision-level metric for cloud invocation, cloud-guidance integration, and request prioritization under deadline and resource constraints. Experiments in CARLA show that SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions while improving planning, efficiency, and navigation success in static and dynamic obstacle scenarios. Compared with fixed-period collaboration, SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions by 50\%, improves navigation success by more than 6\%, and cuts finish time by up to 26.2\% in dynamic scenarios.

OpenDriveLab.title: Video-Conditioned Generative Joint 2D-3D Hand Motion Recovery
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Chen Xu, Yunqi Li, Binbin Huang, Brent Yi, Shenghua Gao
OpenDriveLab.summary: JoHan is a generative framework that recovers 2D and 3D hand motion from video sequences, improving accuracy and temporal consistency without intermediate pose predictions.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Recovering faithful 3D hand motion from video remains challenging due to frequent occlusions and incomplete visual observations, which make frame-wise pose estimates unreliable and temporally inconsistent. The generated 2D trajectories exploit direct spatial and temporal cues from the 2D images to guide the following generative 3D motion reconstruction, while the learned motion prior promotes temporal consistency. Their learned 2D-3D correspondence further enables recovery of the hand's global position and orientation relative to the camera. Extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks demonstrate significantly improved accuracy and speed in local hand-pose and camera-space reconstruction. Notably, our method captures much better hand-motion dynamics, producing significantly smoother motion than previous methods while maintaining high per-frame pose accuracy.

OpenDriveLab.title: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Zihao Zhang, Haochen Tian, Tianyu Li, Changhui Jing, Jingliang He
OpenDriveLab.summary: The paper introduces ViRA, a framework demonstrating that visual foundation models enhance autonomous driving performance, emphasizing the importance of target selection and planner supervision.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Visual foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly integrated into end-to-end autonomous driving for their powerful representations, yet it remains unclear when these representations improve driving performance. To investigate this question, we introduce ViRA, a planner-agnostic visual representation alignment framework that keeps the planner architecture and inference cost unchanged. Our study reveals three findings: (1) VFM-guided visual representations consistently improve driving performance across diverse end-to-end planners, with gains extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation. (2) The choice of VFM target matters for planning performance, and alignment to a different VFM can further benefit planners with pre-trained VFM encoders. (3) Auxiliary perception supervision reduces sensitivity to VFM target selection, narrowing the EPDMS spread across five targets from 2.7 to 0.5 points and potentially compensating for less effective VFM targets. Guided by these findings, we develop ViRA-Diffusion, a diffusion-based planner trained without auxiliary perception supervision, which achieves 92.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest, outperforming recent methods in our comparison by at least 1.9 points. The results motivate jointly considering target selection and planner supervision when integrating VFMs into end-to-end autonomous driving. The results and demo are available at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/ViRA.

OpenDriveLab.title: SAIN: Structure-Aware Interactive Navigation with Active Dialogue Grounding for Mobile Robot
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Yuhao Cao, Xiao Liu, Yang Xie, Lu Liu, Haoyao Chen
OpenDriveLab.summary: SAIN introduces a zero-shot framework for interactive navigation that transforms active dialogue into persistent navigation states, improving performance on ambiguous instructions without task-specific training.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Most existing vision-language navigation tasks assume that instructions are complete and unambiguous. However, real-world robots often encounter natural human instructions that are ambiguous, underspecified, or incomplete, requiring them to resolve such uncertainties through active questioning. Interactive Instance Goal Navigation (IIGN) requires an embodied agent to find the specific instance under an ambiguous category-level instruction through active dialogue. However, existing dialogue-enabled methods often consume oracle answers as transient textual context for immediate decisions, rather than persistent spatial or object-centric structured state. We present SAIN, a zero-shot framework that turns active dialogue into persistent navigation state. Instead of consuming oracle answers as one-step text hints, SAIN compiles them into target evidence, route-level corridor memory, and object-candidate labels. These states are stored in structured value, room, graph, and object memories, then consumed by a unified policy for frontier ranking and final target approach. On the VL-LN IIGN benchmark, SAIN improves SR from 20.2 to 25.4 and SPL from 13.07 to 14.17 over the strongest reported dialogue-enabled baseline, while requiring no task-specific policy training. The results support dialogue-to-state conversion as an effective zero-shot mechanism for long-horizon interactive instance navigation. Project website: https://zorattc.github.io/SAIN/

OpenDriveLab.title: Open-CHOIR: Open-World Contact-Aware 4D Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Hao Xu, Yilin Liu, Yinqiao Wang, Chi-Wing Fu, Niloy J. Mitra
OpenDriveLab.summary: Open-CHOIR is a framework that reconstructs 4D hand-object interactions from monocular videos by utilizing contact as a coupling signal for improved accuracy and consistency.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: We ask whether everyday open-world monocular videos can be turned into reusable 4D interaction primitives: articulated hand motion, object shape with 6D pose over time, and the when/where of contact. Such a capability would enable scalable mining of real interactions and, beyond reconstruction, support scene-aware synthesis and planning. However, reconstructing hand-object interaction (HOI) from challenging monocular videos remains difficult: methods often assume known objects or curated scenes, and separately estimated hands and objects easily become misaligned under clutter, occlusion, and unseen object geometries. Targeting this setting, we present Open-CHOIR, an Open-world Contact-aware HOI Reconstruction framework for a monocular camera, using contact as an explicit coupling signal between hands and objects. Open-CHOIR first initializes a coarse, contact-agnostic 4D HOI sequence from open-world visual priors. It then introduces a generative HOI spatial rectification module to predict ray-depth corrections and rectify hand-object relative placement, then derive initial per-frame contact correspondences on the rectified geometry. Last, a contact-aware joint optimization with dynamically updated contact constraints enforces geometric, temporal, and contact consistency. Experiments on controlled and challenging videos show that Open-CHOIR improves object reconstruction, physical plausibility, and temporal consistency over state-of-the-art methods. Code, data, and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/hxwork/CHOIR.

OpenDriveLab.title: Boosting Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Deep Reinforcement Learning
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Zexin Li, Ruili Yao, Yiming Zeng, Xiaoxue Gao
OpenDriveLab.summary: This paper presents a trajectory-level black-box attack method for deep reinforcement learning that outperforms traditional per-step attacks by optimizing observation perturbations over time.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Most adversarial attacks on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) assume white-box access to the victim policy, which rarely holds in practice. This paper studies transfer-based black-box attacks on DRL: the attacker crafts observation perturbations on a white-box surrogate agent and feeds them to an unknown victim. We formulate the attack as return minimization under a per-step perturbation budget. We first show that transplanting transferable image-classification attacks (FGSM, MI-FGSM, and NI-FGSM) with a per-step objective yields perturbations that transfer but are no stronger than random noise of the same budget. We then propose a trajectory-level attack that optimizes a sequence of perturbations over a receding horizon through a differentiable model of the environment and a temperature-smoothed surrogate policy, with the same optimizers. On CartPole-v1 with ten DQN and DDQN agents and 100 surrogate--victim pairs, the trajectory-level attack outperforms per-step attacks and random noise in the white-box, cross-model, and cross-algorithm settings.

OpenDriveLab.title: $R^2$-WAM: Repair-and-Reject Post-Training for World Action Models
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Ruiyan Xu, Haisheng Su, Sixu Lin, Zhaokun Yue, Chengming Hu
OpenDriveLab.summary: $R^2$-WAM enhances World Action Models by implementing a two-stage repair-and-reject framework to improve action prediction consistency and refine policies without extra interactions.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) emerge as a promising foundation for policy refinement by predicting the consequences of sampled actions. However, visually plausible predictions can mislead policy refinement if they fail to reflect the input actions. To address this mismatch, we introduce $R^2$-WAM, a two-stage repair-and-reject post-training framework that first improves the consistency of predicted futures with input actions, then uses these futures to select inferior action samples for negative fine-tuning. The repair stage grounds imagination in observed robot behavior through a kinematic alignment score that measures agreement between predicted and demonstrated motion, enabling the predicted video to faithfully reflect its input actions. Using the repaired video model, the rejection stage compares imagined outcomes of sampled and demonstrated actions, selectively applying negative fine-tuning to samples whose predicted task progress falls below the demonstrated reference by a prescribed margin. Together, the two stages extend video prediction from representation learning to consequence-based policy refinement without additional environment interaction or changes to the inference procedure. $R^2$-WAM achieves 93.8% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 across clean and randomized settings. On the long-horizon real-world Fold Shirt task, it achieves 87.5% average success, compared with 0% for Fast-WAM. Our project page is available at https://r2-wam.github.io/.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: RollVerify: Bridging Efficiency and Accuracy in Long-Tail Rollout Reinforcement Learning
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yongqiang Yao, Jinru Tan, Kaihuan Liang, Zixin Yin, Yazhe Niu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: RollVerify enhances reinforcement learning efficiency by actively verifying and repairing off-policy samples, achieving on-par accuracy with reduced training costs in long-tail rollouts.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning is crucial for improving large language models' reasoning and generalization. It relies on massive rollouts whose lengths become increasingly long-tailed as context windows grow. In on-policy training, these long-tail rollouts can result in GPU bubbles, reducing system utilization and limiting RL scalability. Asynchronous or partial-rollout methods improve throughput by relaxing synchronization, but inevitably introduce stale off-policy samples (trajectories) that may hurt final accuracy. Existing approaches mainly mitigate this off-policy issue by reweighting off-policy samples during training, yet they can still leave a performance gap compared to fully on-policy training. In this work, rather than passively reweighting samples during training, we propose RollVerify, a lightweight RL framework built on partial rollout that actively verifies and repairs samples before they enter training. Specifically, it introduces an off-policy shift metric OPS, to quantify the off-policy deviation of partially generated trajectories. Guided by the OPS constraint, RollVerify performs both sequence-level and token-level verification to identify and truncate invalid suffixes of trajectories. This yields high-quality samples that protect the models' accuracy while preserving the efficiency gains of partial rollout. Experiments on mathematical and tool-assisted mathematical reasoning show that RollVerify achieves accuracy comparable to on-policy training while reducing training cost. Additional code-generation results provide preliminary evidence beyond mathematics.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: WSM-Aware HRI: An IoT-Enhanced Framework for Early Detection and Norm-Guided Repair of Failures with LLM Guidance
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Hanlin Zhang, Yuquan Wang, Tianwei Zhang, Zhenglong Sun
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The WSM-Aware HRI framework utilizes IoT and LLMs to proactively detect and repair human-robot interaction failures by addressing World-State Mismatches during intention formation.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Human-robot interaction (HRI) failures remain a major barrier to deploying robots in real-world environments. Prior work often treats failures as isolated technical faults or focuses on post-hoc recovery behaviors. In practice, many breakdowns arise because humans and robots operate under inconsistent assumptions about the current world state. We propose WSM-Aware HRI, an IoT-enhanced modular framework that unifies diverse HRI breakdowns as World-State Mismatches (WSMs) between a human's instruction-implied assumptions and a robot's grounded world model built from multimodal perception and digital augmentation. A Large Language Model (LLM) is used to make implicit assumptions explicit, map them to a small set of mismatch types, and specify the evidence needed for verification against the robot's world state. WSM-Aware HRI shifts failure handling from execution-time recovery to proactive mismatch detection during intention formation, enabling interventions guided by safety, norm compliance, and multi-user coordination with transparent explanations. We evaluate mismatch identification in ten everyday cases spanning both visual and latent-state mismatches. The system can accurately produce the expected output results, and ablations show that reliable identification depends on appropriate grounding representations and verification-oriented refinement. These results indicate that treating interaction breakdowns as explicit world-state mismatches enables earlier detection of impending failures and offers a principled mechanism for integrating external evidence and social constraints into human-robot interaction.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: UniSkill: Learning Actor-Aligned Skill Proposals for an Evolving Policy
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yifei Lu, Cheng Liu, Dianzhi Yu, Hui Xiang, Ji Zhang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: UniSkill enhances policy learning by proposing skill edits through a shared policy, leveraging contrastive feedback to optimize skill extraction without costly rollouts.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Large language model agents can improve across tasks by retaining reusable skills distilled from prior interactions. Recent work jointly optimizes task execution and skill extraction, enabling the policy and skillbank to co-evolve. However, as the actor continues learning, rewarding skill proposals through their reuse in subsequent training steps may conflate skill benefits with actor improvement, while directly testing each proposed skill requires costly additional actor rollouts. In this paper, we introduce UniSkill, which uses a shared policy to interact with the environment and propose skillbank edits (Add, Update, or No Edit) from the resulting trajectories. Specifically, the actor learns from environment rewards, while contrastive action feedback guides skill proposal learning. This feedback provides an actor-alignment signal by measuring how replacing the retrieved skill with a proposed skill changes the current actor's action log-likelihood gap between previously collected successful and failed trajectories from the same task, thereby avoiding new rollouts for each proposal. Since proposal-level feedback may suppress an otherwise appropriate edit operation when the proposed skill content scores poorly, we further apply skill-edit support regularization to preserve exploration. Empirically, UniSkill achieves strong performance, reaching 98.4% success on ALFWorld and 84.7% on WebShop while maintaining stable joint training. Further ALFWorld experiments show that UniSkill remains effective when the shared policy uses a smaller backbone. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/LimOkii/UniSKill.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Beyond Reward Suppression: Near-Optimal Offline Attacks on Warm-Start Bandits with Bounded Rewards
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Qirun Zeng, Manhin Poon, Xiangxiang Dai, Qixin Zhang, Jinhang Zuo
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper presents a novel approach to offline attacks on warm-start bandits, demonstrating that promoting target arms is essential for effective adversarial manipulation while minimizing costs.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Adversarial attacks on bandits aim to mislead a learner toward a target arm while keeping the attack cost small. Existing attacks typically achieve this by suppressing non-target arms. In practice, however, manipulation such as fake reviews often directly promotes the target item. We study this gap through bounded offline attacks on warm-start bandits, where an attacker can inject only valid action-reward pairs into the warm-start history before deployment. We show that target promotion is not merely a heuristic: when the target arm lies near the lower reward boundary, any order-optimal-cost attack against UCB that makes it selected in nearly all online rounds must allocate a nonvanishing fraction of its cost to the target arm. We then design an attack that achieves the optimal sublinear cost and characterize its allocation between target promotion and non-target suppression. We further extend the attack to Thompson Sampling, $ε$-greedy, and a broader class of bandit algorithms. Experiments on real-world and synthetic data validate the effectiveness of our attacks.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: UltraWorld: Learning Interactive Ultrasound World Models from Untracked Clinical Videos with Acoustic Sampling Map
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Keke Yang, Erqi Wang, Sainan Guan, Hongliang Ren
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: UltraWorld enables autonomous ultrasound scanning by creating interactive world models from untracked clinical videos, enhancing action prediction and following through synthetic data and Acoustic Sampling Maps.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: World models can enable autonomous ultrasound scanning by predicting the outcomes of probe motions from local observations. Learning this action--observation relationship typically relies on synchronized video--pose pairs, which are costly to collect at scale and largely unavailable in routine clinical recordings. Reliable action following further requires modeling ultrasound's cross-sectional sampling geometry. We present UltraWorld, a self-distillation recipe that transfers priors from clinical ultrasound videos into interactive world models without real action annotations. Starting from clinical videos, we adapt a video foundation model into an ultrasound generator conditioned on reference images and anatomical masks. We then use these synthetic pairs to self-distill the generator into a world model that predicts future observations from local observations and actions, without requiring anatomical masks or other 3D assets at inference time. Experiments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity and action following. Project Page: https://ultraworld-project.github.io/.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: TriDeliver: Cooperative Air-Ground Instant Delivery with UAVs, Couriers, and Crowdsourced Ground Vehicles
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Junhui Gao, Yan Pan, Qianru Wang, Wenzhe Hou, Yiqin Deng
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: TriDeliver introduces a hierarchical framework combining UAVs, couriers, and crowdsourced ground vehicles, enhancing instant delivery efficiency and reducing costs significantly through transfer learning.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Instant delivery, shipping items before critical deadlines, is essential in daily life. While multiple delivery agents, such as couriers, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), and crowdsourced agents, have been widely employed, each of them faces inherent limitations (e.g., low efficiency/labor shortages, flight control, and dynamic capabilities, respectively), preventing them from meeting the surging demands alone. This paper proposes TriDeliver, the first hierarchical cooperative framework, integrating human couriers, UAVs, and crowdsourced ground vehicles (GVs) for efficient instant delivery. To obtain the initial scheduling knowledge for GVs and UAVs as well as improve the cooperative delivery performance, we design a Transfer Learning (TL)-based algorithm to extract delivery knowledge from couriers' behavioral history and transfer their knowledge to UAVs and GVs with fine-tunings, which is then used to dispatch parcels for efficient delivery. Evaluated on one-month real-world trajectory and delivery datasets, it has been demonstrated that 1) by integrating couriers, UAVs, and crowdsourced GVs, TriDeliver reduces the delivery cost by $65.8\%$ versus state-of-the-art cooperative delivery by UAVs and couriers; 2) TriDeliver achieves further improvements in terms of delivery time ($-17.7\%$), delivery cost ($-9.8\%$), and impacts on original tasks of crowdsourced GVs ($-43.6\%$), even with the representation of the transferred knowledge by simple neural networks, respectively.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: MagCilia: A Compact Magnetociliary Tactile Sensor with 3D Force Sensing for Robotic Contact Perception and Grasping Feedback
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yu Feng, Hao Wu, Haotian Guo, Haoming Liu, William Su
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The MagCilia sensor enables precise 3D force sensing and surface recognition for robotic grasping through a compact design integrating flexible magnetic-cilia structures and advanced data fusion techniques.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Robotic grasping and surface exploration benefit from simultaneous measurement of normal and tangential forces and from surface information obtained through contact. Here, we present a compact magnetociliary tactile sensor (MagCilia) that combines a flexible magnetic-cilia structure with a Hall sensor for 3D force sensing. Quasi-static finite element analysis is used to investigate structural deformation and magnetic responses under multidirectional loading. To reconstruct forces from the coupled magnetic channels, we propose causal history fusion regression (CHFR), which combines current magnetic-field measurements with their recent changes. Five-fold cross-validation grouped by calibration record yields root-mean-square errors of 0.40, 0.57, and 0.69 N for Fx, Fy, and Fz, respectively, with corresponding coefficients of determination of 0.93, 0.90, and 0.92. Robotic experiments demonstrate tangential-force-guided gripper adjustment and multi-axis load monitoring under external perturbations. Frequency-domain features of the reconstructed forces distinguish six surface categories with 99.39% accuracy in three-fold cross-validation grouped by acquisition session. An online robotic demonstration additionally identifies all six tested surfaces. These results demonstrate 3D force reconstruction, grasping feedback, and surface recognition using a single compact tactile unit.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Not All Uncertainty Matters: Simulation-in-the-Loop Fast-Slow Reasoning for Decision-Critical Autonomous Driving System
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Jiayi Chen, Shuai Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Chengzhong Xu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents SIGMA, a simulation-in-the-loop framework that optimizes cloud interactions for autonomous driving by assessing uncertainty's impact on planning efficiency and decision-making.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) provide powerful open-world perception and reasoning for autonomous driving, but their high computational cost and inference latency make continuous cloud-side use impractical. This motivates fast--slow collaboration, where efficient onboard modules handle real-time perception and control while cloud models provide high-level reasoning only when needed. The key challenge is deciding when cloud reasoning should influence time-critical driving decisions. Existing methods often rely on perception uncertainty, heuristic triggers, or resource-driven policies, without assessing whether resolving an uncertainty will improve planning. We propose \textbf{SIGMA}, a simulation-in-the-loop framework for task-oriented fast--slow collaboration. SIGMA embeds the planner into uncertainty assessment and evaluates how plausible scene realizations under semantic and geometric uncertainty affect feasible trajectories and planning cost. Based on these outcomes, it estimates the expected reduction in planning cost from resolving uncertainty. We further introduce expected planning gain (EPG), a decision-level metric for cloud invocation, cloud-guidance integration, and request prioritization under deadline and resource constraints. Experiments in CARLA show that SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions while improving planning, efficiency, and navigation success in static and dynamic obstacle scenarios. Compared with fixed-period collaboration, SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions by 50\%, improves navigation success by more than 6\%, and cuts finish time by up to 26.2\% in dynamic scenarios.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: WSM-Aware HRI: An IoT-Enhanced Framework for Early Detection and Norm-Guided Repair of Failures with LLM Guidance
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Hanlin Zhang, Yuquan Wang, Tianwei Zhang, Zhenglong Sun
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The WSM-Aware HRI framework utilizes IoT and LLMs to proactively detect and repair human-robot interaction failures by addressing World-State Mismatches during intention formation.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Human-robot interaction (HRI) failures remain a major barrier to deploying robots in real-world environments. Prior work often treats failures as isolated technical faults or focuses on post-hoc recovery behaviors. In practice, many breakdowns arise because humans and robots operate under inconsistent assumptions about the current world state. We propose WSM-Aware HRI, an IoT-enhanced modular framework that unifies diverse HRI breakdowns as World-State Mismatches (WSMs) between a human's instruction-implied assumptions and a robot's grounded world model built from multimodal perception and digital augmentation. A Large Language Model (LLM) is used to make implicit assumptions explicit, map them to a small set of mismatch types, and specify the evidence needed for verification against the robot's world state. WSM-Aware HRI shifts failure handling from execution-time recovery to proactive mismatch detection during intention formation, enabling interventions guided by safety, norm compliance, and multi-user coordination with transparent explanations. We evaluate mismatch identification in ten everyday cases spanning both visual and latent-state mismatches. The system can accurately produce the expected output results, and ablations show that reliable identification depends on appropriate grounding representations and verification-oriented refinement. These results indicate that treating interaction breakdowns as explicit world-state mismatches enables earlier detection of impending failures and offers a principled mechanism for integrating external evidence and social constraints into human-robot interaction.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Video-Conditioned Generative Joint 2D-3D Hand Motion Recovery
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Chen Xu, Yunqi Li, Binbin Huang, Brent Yi, Shenghua Gao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: JoHan is a generative framework that recovers 2D and 3D hand motion from video sequences, improving accuracy and temporal consistency without intermediate pose predictions.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Recovering faithful 3D hand motion from video remains challenging due to frequent occlusions and incomplete visual observations, which make frame-wise pose estimates unreliable and temporally inconsistent. To address this problem, we propose JoHan, a unified generative framework that recovers hand motion directly from video sequences without relying on intermediate per-frame pose predictions. Trained from scratch, our model jointly generates aligned 2D and 3D local hand pose sequences by learning their temporal dynamics and cross-representation correspondence. The generated 2D trajectories exploit direct spatial and temporal cues from the 2D images to guide the following generative 3D motion reconstruction, while the learned motion prior promotes temporal consistency. Their learned 2D-3D correspondence further enables recovery of the hand's global position and orientation relative to the camera. Extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks demonstrate significantly improved accuracy and speed in local hand-pose and camera-space reconstruction. Notably, our method captures much better hand-motion dynamics, producing significantly smoother motion than previous methods while maintaining high per-frame pose accuracy.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: UniSkill: Learning Actor-Aligned Skill Proposals for an Evolving Policy
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yifei Lu, Cheng Liu, Dianzhi Yu, Hui Xiang, Ji Zhang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: UniSkill enhances policy learning by proposing skill edits through a shared policy, leveraging contrastive feedback to optimize skill extraction without costly rollouts.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model agents can improve across tasks by retaining reusable skills distilled from prior interactions. Recent work jointly optimizes task execution and skill extraction, enabling the policy and skillbank to co-evolve. However, as the actor continues learning, rewarding skill proposals through their reuse in subsequent training steps may conflate skill benefits with actor improvement, while directly testing each proposed skill requires costly additional actor rollouts. In this paper, we introduce UniSkill, which uses a shared policy to interact with the environment and propose skillbank edits (Add, Update, or No Edit) from the resulting trajectories. Specifically, the actor learns from environment rewards, while contrastive action feedback guides skill proposal learning. This feedback provides an actor-alignment signal by measuring how replacing the retrieved skill with a proposed skill changes the current actor's action log-likelihood gap between previously collected successful and failed trajectories from the same task, thereby avoiding new rollouts for each proposal. Since proposal-level feedback may suppress an otherwise appropriate edit operation when the proposed skill content scores poorly, we further apply skill-edit support regularization to preserve exploration. Empirically, UniSkill achieves strong performance, reaching 98.4% success on ALFWorld and 84.7% on WebShop while maintaining stable joint training. Further ALFWorld experiments show that UniSkill remains effective when the shared policy uses a smaller backbone. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/LimOkii/UniSKill.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Beyond Reward Suppression: Near-Optimal Offline Attacks on Warm-Start Bandits with Bounded Rewards
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Qirun Zeng, Manhin Poon, Xiangxiang Dai, Qixin Zhang, Jinhang Zuo
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents a novel approach to offline attacks on warm-start bandits, demonstrating that promoting target arms is essential for effective adversarial manipulation while minimizing costs.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Adversarial attacks on bandits aim to mislead a learner toward a target arm while keeping the attack cost small. Existing attacks typically achieve this by suppressing non-target arms. In practice, however, manipulation such as fake reviews often directly promotes the target item. We study this gap through bounded offline attacks on warm-start bandits, where an attacker can inject only valid action-reward pairs into the warm-start history before deployment. We show that target promotion is not merely a heuristic: when the target arm lies near the lower reward boundary, any order-optimal-cost attack against UCB that makes it selected in nearly all online rounds must allocate a nonvanishing fraction of its cost to the target arm. We then design an attack that achieves the optimal sublinear cost and characterize its allocation between target promotion and non-target suppression. We further extend the attack to Thompson Sampling, $ε$-greedy, and a broader class of bandit algorithms. Experiments on real-world and synthetic data validate the effectiveness of our attacks.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: UltraWorld: Learning Interactive Ultrasound World Models from Untracked Clinical Videos with Acoustic Sampling Map
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Keke Yang, Erqi Wang, Sainan Guan, Hongliang Ren
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: UltraWorld enables autonomous ultrasound scanning by creating interactive world models from untracked clinical videos, enhancing action prediction and following through synthetic data and Acoustic Sampling Maps.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: World models can enable autonomous ultrasound scanning by predicting the outcomes of probe motions from local observations. Learning this action--observation relationship typically relies on synchronized video--pose pairs, which are costly to collect at scale and largely unavailable in routine clinical recordings. Reliable action following further requires modeling ultrasound's cross-sectional sampling geometry. We present UltraWorld, a self-distillation recipe that transfers priors from clinical ultrasound videos into interactive world models without real action annotations. Starting from clinical videos, we adapt a video foundation model into an ultrasound generator conditioned on reference images and anatomical masks. Anatomical masks sampled along programmable trajectories through 3D anatomy provide spatial guidance for synthesizing action--video pairs. We then use these synthetic pairs to self-distill the generator into a world model that predicts future observations from local observations and actions, without requiring anatomical masks or other 3D assets at inference time. To further improve action following, we introduce the Acoustic Sampling Map (AsMap), which represents probe poses and imaging settings as pixel-wise 3D sampling positions, beam directions, and depths. Experiments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity and action following. Across nine simulated closed-loop local planning episodes, UltraWorld reduces the mean final distance to the goal and orientation error by 29\% and 38\%, respectively, compared with visual servoing. Project Page: https://ultraworld-project.github.io/.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Zihao Zhang, Haochen Tian, Tianyu Li, Changhui Jing, Jingliang He
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces ViRA, a framework demonstrating that visual foundation models enhance autonomous driving performance, emphasizing the importance of target selection and planner supervision.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Visual foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly integrated into end-to-end autonomous driving for their powerful representations, yet it remains unclear when these representations improve driving performance. To investigate this question, we introduce ViRA, a planner-agnostic visual representation alignment framework that keeps the planner architecture and inference cost unchanged. Our study reveals three findings: (1) VFM-guided visual representations consistently improve driving performance across diverse end-to-end planners, with gains extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation. (2) The choice of VFM target matters for planning performance, and alignment to a different VFM can further benefit planners with pre-trained VFM encoders. (3) Auxiliary perception supervision reduces sensitivity to VFM target selection, narrowing the EPDMS spread across five targets from 2.7 to 0.5 points and potentially compensating for less effective VFM targets. Guided by these findings, we develop ViRA-Diffusion, a diffusion-based planner trained without auxiliary perception supervision, which achieves 92.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest, outperforming recent methods in our comparison by at least 1.9 points. The results motivate jointly considering target selection and planner supervision when integrating VFMs into end-to-end autonomous driving. The results and demo are available at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/ViRA.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: WAMJET: A Harness for World Action Model Acceleration
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Le Chen, Lixin Liu, Jan Schneider, Zeju Qiu, Simon Guist
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: WAMJET is an innovative harness that accelerates World Action Model inference by optimizing coding agents through a bottleneck-driven workflow, achieving up to 9.95x speedup while maintaining action quality.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) leverage pretrained video foundation models for robot manipulation, but their large backbones and video-action co-prediction are expensive. Although existing acceleration techniques offer many ways to reduce this cost, selecting and composing them requires substantial engineering for each model and hardware platform. To tackle this bottleneck, we present WAMJET, an agentic harness that accelerates WAM inference by equipping coding agents with reusable optimization guidance and measurement and validation tools. WAMJET follows a bottleneck-driven workflow where the agent profiles inference, modifies targeted code, validates effects, and iteratively refines the acceleration stack as bottlenecks shift, while preserving action quality. Experiments span six WAMs, three coding agents, and two GPU architectures. WAMJET achieves up to 9.95x lossless speedup over upstream implementations. Approximation and hardware-aware optimization yield additional latency reductions, with comparable success rates. The results show that WAMJET can produce effective acceleration stacks for WAM deployment.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: SAIN: Structure-Aware Interactive Navigation with Active Dialogue Grounding for Mobile Robot
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yuhao Cao, Xiao Liu, Yang Xie, Lu Liu, Haoyao Chen
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: SAIN introduces a zero-shot framework for interactive navigation that transforms active dialogue into persistent navigation states, improving performance on ambiguous instructions without task-specific training.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Most existing vision-language navigation tasks assume that instructions are complete and unambiguous. However, real-world robots often encounter natural human instructions that are ambiguous, underspecified, or incomplete, requiring them to resolve such uncertainties through active questioning. Interactive Instance Goal Navigation (IIGN) requires an embodied agent to find the specific instance under an ambiguous category-level instruction through active dialogue. However, existing dialogue-enabled methods often consume oracle answers as transient textual context for immediate decisions, rather than persistent spatial or object-centric structured state. We present SAIN, a zero-shot framework that turns active dialogue into persistent navigation state. Instead of consuming oracle answers as one-step text hints, SAIN compiles them into target evidence, route-level corridor memory, and object-candidate labels. These states are stored in structured value, room, graph, and object memories, then consumed by a unified policy for frontier ranking and final target approach. On the VL-LN IIGN benchmark, SAIN improves SR from 20.2 to 25.4 and SPL from 13.07 to 14.17 over the strongest reported dialogue-enabled baseline, while requiring no task-specific policy training. The results support dialogue-to-state conversion as an effective zero-shot mechanism for long-horizon interactive instance navigation. Project website: https://zorattc.github.io/SAIN/

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Open-CHOIR: Open-World Contact-Aware 4D Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Hao Xu, Yilin Liu, Yinqiao Wang, Chi-Wing Fu, Niloy J. Mitra
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Open-CHOIR is a framework that reconstructs 4D hand-object interactions from monocular videos by utilizing contact as a coupling signal for improved accuracy and consistency.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: We ask whether everyday open-world monocular videos can be turned into reusable 4D interaction primitives: articulated hand motion, object shape with 6D pose over time, and the when/where of contact. Such a capability would enable scalable mining of real interactions and, beyond reconstruction, support scene-aware synthesis and planning. However, reconstructing hand-object interaction (HOI) from challenging monocular videos remains difficult: methods often assume known objects or curated scenes, and separately estimated hands and objects easily become misaligned under clutter, occlusion, and unseen object geometries. Targeting this setting, we present Open-CHOIR, an Open-world Contact-aware HOI Reconstruction framework for a monocular camera, using contact as an explicit coupling signal between hands and objects. Open-CHOIR first initializes a coarse, contact-agnostic 4D HOI sequence from open-world visual priors. It then introduces a generative HOI spatial rectification module to predict ray-depth corrections and rectify hand-object relative placement, then derive initial per-frame contact correspondences on the rectified geometry. Last, a contact-aware joint optimization with dynamically updated contact constraints enforces geometric, temporal, and contact consistency. Experiments on controlled and challenging videos show that Open-CHOIR improves object reconstruction, physical plausibility, and temporal consistency over state-of-the-art methods. Code, data, and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/hxwork/CHOIR.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Boosting Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Deep Reinforcement Learning
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Zexin Li, Ruili Yao, Yiming Zeng, Xiaoxue Gao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: This paper presents a trajectory-level black-box attack method for deep reinforcement learning that outperforms traditional per-step attacks by optimizing observation perturbations over time.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Most adversarial attacks on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) assume white-box access to the victim policy, which rarely holds in practice. This paper studies transfer-based black-box attacks on DRL: the attacker crafts observation perturbations on a white-box surrogate agent and feeds them to an unknown victim. We formulate the attack as return minimization under a per-step perturbation budget. We first show that transplanting transferable image-classification attacks (FGSM, MI-FGSM, and NI-FGSM) with a per-step objective yields perturbations that transfer but are no stronger than random noise of the same budget. We then propose a trajectory-level attack that optimizes a sequence of perturbations over a receding horizon through a differentiable model of the environment and a temperature-smoothed surrogate policy, with the same optimizers. On CartPole-v1 with ten DQN and DDQN agents and 100 surrogate--victim pairs, the trajectory-level attack outperforms per-step attacks and random noise in the white-box, cross-model, and cross-algorithm settings.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: $R^2$-WAM: Repair-and-Reject Post-Training for World Action Models
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Ruiyan Xu, Haisheng Su, Sixu Lin, Zhaokun Yue, Chengming Hu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: $R^2$-WAM enhances World Action Models by implementing a two-stage repair-and-reject framework to improve action prediction consistency and refine policies without extra interactions.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) emerge as a promising foundation for policy refinement by predicting the consequences of sampled actions. However, visually plausible predictions can mislead policy refinement if they fail to reflect the input actions. To address this mismatch, we introduce $R^2$-WAM, a two-stage repair-and-reject post-training framework that first improves the consistency of predicted futures with input actions, then uses these futures to select inferior action samples for negative fine-tuning. The repair stage grounds imagination in observed robot behavior through a kinematic alignment score that measures agreement between predicted and demonstrated motion, enabling the predicted video to faithfully reflect its input actions. Using the repaired video model, the rejection stage compares imagined outcomes of sampled and demonstrated actions, selectively applying negative fine-tuning to samples whose predicted task progress falls below the demonstrated reference by a prescribed margin. Together, the two stages extend video prediction from representation learning to consequence-based policy refinement without additional environment interaction or changes to the inference procedure. $R^2$-WAM achieves 93.8% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 across clean and randomized settings. On the long-horizon real-world Fold Shirt task, it achieves 87.5% average success, compared with 0% for Fast-WAM. Our project page is available at https://r2-wam.github.io/.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: RollVerify: Bridging Efficiency and Accuracy in Long-Tail Rollout Reinforcement Learning
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yongqiang Yao, Jinru Tan, Kaihuan Liang, Zixin Yin, Yazhe Niu
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: RollVerify enhances reinforcement learning efficiency by actively verifying and repairing off-policy samples, achieving on-par accuracy with reduced training costs in long-tail rollouts.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning is crucial for improving large language models' reasoning and generalization. It relies on massive rollouts whose lengths become increasingly long-tailed as context windows grow. In on-policy training, these long-tail rollouts can result in GPU bubbles, reducing system utilization and limiting RL scalability. Asynchronous or partial-rollout methods improve throughput by relaxing synchronization, but inevitably introduce stale off-policy samples (trajectories) that may hurt final accuracy. Existing approaches mainly mitigate this off-policy issue by reweighting off-policy samples during training, yet they can still leave a performance gap compared to fully on-policy training. In this work, rather than passively reweighting samples during training, we propose RollVerify, a lightweight RL framework built on partial rollout that actively verifies and repairs samples before they enter training. Specifically, it introduces an off-policy shift metric OPS, to quantify the off-policy deviation of partially generated trajectories. Guided by the OPS constraint, RollVerify performs both sequence-level and token-level verification to identify and truncate invalid suffixes of trajectories. This yields high-quality samples that protect the models' accuracy while preserving the efficiency gains of partial rollout. Experiments on mathematical and tool-assisted mathematical reasoning show that RollVerify achieves accuracy comparable to on-policy training while reducing training cost. Additional code-generation results provide preliminary evidence beyond mathematics.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: TriDeliver: Cooperative Air-Ground Instant Delivery with UAVs, Couriers, and Crowdsourced Ground Vehicles
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Junhui Gao, Yan Pan, Qianru Wang, Wenzhe Hou, Yiqin Deng
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: TriDeliver introduces a hierarchical framework combining UAVs, couriers, and crowdsourced ground vehicles, enhancing instant delivery efficiency and reducing costs significantly through transfer learning.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Instant delivery, shipping items before critical deadlines, is essential in daily life. While multiple delivery agents, such as couriers, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), and crowdsourced agents, have been widely employed, each of them faces inherent limitations (e.g., low efficiency/labor shortages, flight control, and dynamic capabilities, respectively), preventing them from meeting the surging demands alone. This paper proposes TriDeliver, the first hierarchical cooperative framework, integrating human couriers, UAVs, and crowdsourced ground vehicles (GVs) for efficient instant delivery. To obtain the initial scheduling knowledge for GVs and UAVs as well as improve the cooperative delivery performance, we design a Transfer Learning (TL)-based algorithm to extract delivery knowledge from couriers' behavioral history and transfer their knowledge to UAVs and GVs with fine-tunings, which is then used to dispatch parcels for efficient delivery. Evaluated on one-month real-world trajectory and delivery datasets, it has been demonstrated that 1) by integrating couriers, UAVs, and crowdsourced GVs, TriDeliver reduces the delivery cost by $65.8\%$ versus state-of-the-art cooperative delivery by UAVs and couriers; 2) TriDeliver achieves further improvements in terms of delivery time ($-17.7\%$), delivery cost ($-9.8\%$), and impacts on original tasks of crowdsourced GVs ($-43.6\%$), even with the representation of the transferred knowledge by simple neural networks, respectively.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: MagCilia: A Compact Magnetociliary Tactile Sensor with 3D Force Sensing for Robotic Contact Perception and Grasping Feedback
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Yu Feng, Hao Wu, Haotian Guo, Haoming Liu, William Su
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The MagCilia sensor enables precise 3D force sensing and surface recognition for robotic grasping through a compact design integrating flexible magnetic-cilia structures and advanced data fusion techniques.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Robotic grasping and surface exploration benefit from simultaneous measurement of normal and tangential forces and from surface information obtained through contact. Here, we present a compact magnetociliary tactile sensor (MagCilia) that combines a flexible magnetic-cilia structure with a Hall sensor for 3D force sensing. Quasi-static finite element analysis is used to investigate structural deformation and magnetic responses under multidirectional loading. To reconstruct forces from the coupled magnetic channels, we propose causal history fusion regression (CHFR), which combines current magnetic-field measurements with their recent changes. Five-fold cross-validation grouped by calibration record yields root-mean-square errors of 0.40, 0.57, and 0.69 N for Fx, Fy, and Fz, respectively, with corresponding coefficients of determination of 0.93, 0.90, and 0.92. Robotic experiments demonstrate tangential-force-guided gripper adjustment and multi-axis load monitoring under external perturbations. Frequency-domain features of the reconstructed forces distinguish six surface categories with 99.39% accuracy in three-fold cross-validation grouped by acquisition session. An online robotic demonstration additionally identifies all six tested surfaces. These results demonstrate 3D force reconstruction, grasping feedback, and surface recognition using a single compact tactile unit.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Not All Uncertainty Matters: Simulation-in-the-Loop Fast-Slow Reasoning for Decision-Critical Autonomous Driving System
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Jiayi Chen, Shuai Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Chengzhong Xu
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents SIGMA, a simulation-in-the-loop framework that optimizes cloud interactions for autonomous driving by assessing uncertainty's impact on planning efficiency and decision-making.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) provide powerful open-world perception and reasoning for autonomous driving, but their high computational cost and inference latency make continuous cloud-side use impractical. This motivates fast--slow collaboration, where efficient onboard modules handle real-time perception and control while cloud models provide high-level reasoning only when needed. The key challenge is deciding when cloud reasoning should influence time-critical driving decisions. Existing methods often rely on perception uncertainty, heuristic triggers, or resource-driven policies, without assessing whether resolving an uncertainty will improve planning. We propose \textbf{SIGMA}, a simulation-in-the-loop framework for task-oriented fast--slow collaboration. SIGMA embeds the planner into uncertainty assessment and evaluates how plausible scene realizations under semantic and geometric uncertainty affect feasible trajectories and planning cost. Based on these outcomes, it estimates the expected reduction in planning cost from resolving uncertainty. We further introduce expected planning gain (EPG), a decision-level metric for cloud invocation, cloud-guidance integration, and request prioritization under deadline and resource constraints. Experiments in CARLA show that SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions while improving planning, efficiency, and navigation success in static and dynamic obstacle scenarios. Compared with fixed-period collaboration, SIGMA reduces unnecessary cloud interactions by 50\%, improves navigation success by more than 6\%, and cuts finish time by up to 26.2\% in dynamic scenarios.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Qirun Zeng, Manhin Poon, Xiangxiang Dai, Qixin Zhang, Jinhang Zuo
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a novel approach to offline attacks on warm-start bandits, demonstrating that promoting target arms is essential for effective adversarial manipulation while minimizing costs.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Adversarial attacks on bandits aim to mislead a learner toward a target arm while keeping the attack cost small. We then design an attack that achieves the optimal sublinear cost and characterize its allocation between target promotion and non-target suppression. We further extend the attack to Thompson Sampling, $ε$-greedy, and a broader class of bandit algorithms. Experiments on real-world and synthetic data validate the effectiveness of our attacks.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: UltraWorld: Learning Interactive Ultrasound World Models from Untracked Clinical Videos with Acoustic Sampling Map
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Keke Yang, Erqi Wang, Sainan Guan, Hongliang Ren
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: UltraWorld enables autonomous ultrasound scanning by creating interactive world models from untracked clinical videos, enhancing action prediction and following through synthetic data and Acoustic Sampling Maps.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: World models can enable autonomous ultrasound scanning by predicting the outcomes of probe motions from local observations. Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.title: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Zihao Zhang, Haochen Tian, Tianyu Li, Changhui Jing, Jingliang He
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces ViRA, a framework demonstrating that visual foundation models enhance autonomous driving performance, emphasizing the importance of target selection and planner supervision.

Our study reveals three findings: (1) VFM-guided visual representations consistently improve driving performance across diverse end-to-end planners, with gains extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation. (3) Auxiliary perception supervision reduces sensitivity to VFM target selection, narrowing the EPDMS spread across five targets from 2.7 to 0.5 points and potentially compensating for less effective VFM targets. The results and demo are available at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/ViRA.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Le Chen, Lixin Liu, Jan Schneider, Zeju Qiu, Simon Guist
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.summary: WAMJET is an innovative harness that accelerates World Action Model inference by optimizing coding agents through a bottleneck-driven workflow, achieving up to 9.95x speedup while maintaining action quality.
Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) leverage pretrained video foundation models for robot manipulation, but their large backbones and video-action co-prediction are expensive. WAMJET follows a bottleneck-driven workflow where the agent profiles inference, modifies targeted code, validates effects, and iteratively refines the acceleration stack as bottlenecks shift, while preserving action quality.
